name: Removing the defender
goal: You can win a piece by taking or chasing away its only defender, or by giving that defender two jobs at once.
intro: Many pieces are safe only because one other piece protects them. Take that protector away and the piece is left hanging. You can capture the defender, chase it off with a pawn, or spot a defender that protects two things at once and cannot do both jobs.

parts.title: Capture the defender
parts.keyIdea: If a piece has only one defender, capture the defender and the piece is left unprotected.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black's bishop has just come to g4, where it attacks your queen. Before you move the queen away, look at what protects that bishop.

notes.text: Your knight takes the knight on f6, the only piece protecting the bishop on g4, and it comes with check. Whatever Black does now, the bishop has lost its guard.
Black took back with the queen, which does not protect g4. Your queen takes the bishop: you have traded knights and won a bishop on top.

parts.title: Chase the defender away
parts.keyIdea: Attack a defender with a pawn: when it runs away, the piece it was guarding is left alone.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. White's knight has just jumped to g5. Your queen on e7 attacks it, but White's queen on e3 protects it.

notes.text: The pawn attacks White's queen, and it also stands on the line from e3 to g5. White's queen has to move, and no square it can safely go to protects the knight.
The queen has stepped away, and the knight on g5 has no protection left. Take it: you are a piece ahead.

parts.title: One defender, two jobs
parts.keyIdea: When one piece guards two things, take one of them; if the defender takes back, the other is left unguarded.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. Black's queen has just come to d4, offering a trade of queens. Look at Black's rook on d8: how many pieces is it protecting?

notes.text: Take the queen. Black's rook on d8 is the only piece that can take back, and it is also the only guard of the rook on c8.
The rook on d8 took back on d4 and left the rook on c8 unprotected. Take it with check: you have won a whole rook.
